tr.td: Establishing primary care: accessible care for a blind adult, recovery-oriented review, and depression and safety screening
Four-week follow-up with ophthalmology consultation for the blind eyes
Three-month review of recovery, accessibility, and fall prevention
Six-month review with depression screening and a plan for any future pain

Disability-competent care at every visit: introductions and spoken orientation, describing each step of the examination, offering an arm for guiding, and all documents in an accessible electronic format
Ophthalmology consultation to examine the blind eyes for comfort and complications and to advise on pressure checks and surveillance

Recovery-oriented care: ask about cravings, triggers, and any return to use at each visit in a non-judgmental way; naloxone at home and when traveling; recovery supports he can reach; and a written plan for any future pain
Depression screening with the PHQ-9 at intake and at six months, PHQ-2 at the wellness visit, and a safety review with the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at each visit
Medicine labeling: audio labels from the pharmacy, a braille label on the naloxone, and the same pharmacy for every prescription
Fall prevention: CDC STEADI screen at each visit, keeping the home layout unchanged, and a sighted guide in unfamiliar places
Visit summaries, results, and medicine information delivered in an accessible electronic format, and medicine labels in braille or audio, by the four-week visit
Visit summaries sent as accessible documents; the pharmacy provides audio labels and a braille label on the naloxone
Naloxone at home and in his travel bag, with a tactile label, and the people he travels with shown how to use it, by the three-month visit
Naloxone in both places; travel staff shown how to use it
Stay in sustained remission, with no return to opioid use, through six months
No opioid use; DAST-10 0 at intake and no use reported at each visit
A written plan for any future acute pain or surgery that uses non-opioid treatment first and builds in safeguards if an opioid is ever needed, by the six-month visit
Plan written with him and saved in an accessible format

list.item: Blind since childhood, with no light perception. Independent in all activities of daily living and instrumental activities using nonvisual methods; uses a screen reader and a smartphone voice assistant; uses a sighted guide in unfamiliar places [S]

Falls: none in the past year and no fear of falling. Timed Up and Go 10 seconds, walking independently along the clinic corridor after a brief spoken orientation; steady gait; no fall in blood pressure on standing (128/78 seated, 126/78 standing) [S]

Access needs: staff introduce themselves, say when they enter or leave the room, describe each step of the examination before touching him, and offer an arm rather than steering him. All written material as accessible electronic documents his screen reader can read; medicine labels in braille or audio [S]
Alert and oriented; warm, witty, and engaged; thought process organized; no signs of intoxication or withdrawal [S]
Mood good; PHQ-9 score 2 with item 9 scored 0; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm [S]

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-03-03: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Routine outpatient care. Crisis resources, including the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, given in an accessible electronic format and saved in his phone; safety reviewed at each visit [S]
